newsitem.title: UK: Tesco, food retailers off on Hoare comment.
newsitem.headline: Tesco, food retailers off on Hoare comment.

text.p: Shares in leading food retailers dropped on Monday as analysts at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett repeated an "overvalued" rating on the sector, market sources said.
Traders also said there was talk that Tesco was planning a new price initiative but a spokeswoman for the company was not aware of any new campaign.
Tesco was down 3p at 300 by 1016 GMT, J. Sainsbury Plc was down 5p at 386-1/2, Safeway Plc was down 5p at 337 and Asda Group Plc was down 1-1/2p at 111.
Analysts at Hoare Govett confirmed they had reiterated their overvalued view on the sector but declined further comment.

Other analysts said there was no immediate reason to believe any fresh Tesco price cuts would be of significant concern to the sector, though an outbreak of discounting could provide an uncertain backdrop for the shares.
"At the end of the day autumn always does see a sharpening in price promotion activity," said one, "and Tesco is likely to be at the forefront.
"We will just have to wait and see if there is anything like last year's campaign which focused on fresh produce."
